tasks.title: Inverted Index Keyword Search Engine
tasks.problem_description: Build an inverted index over a collection of short text documents and answer single-keyword and multi-keyword AND queries against it. The solution must be implemented as pure, offline, deterministic Python runnable in a single Jupyter/Colab cell with no network or human interaction.
functional_requirements: R1: Correctly build the required index/data structure described for 'Inverted Index Keyword Search Engine' from the given input collection.
R2: Correctly answer a single query against the built structure, returning results in the specified deterministic order.
R3: Correctly handle an empty query or empty input collection by returning an empty result rather than raising an exception.
R4: Support repeated/duplicate queries returning consistent results without mutating the underlying index.
R5: Scale to large input sizes without falling back to a full linear rescan per query where an index lookup is specified by the algorithm.
R6: Return results using only the documented input/output types (no extra I/O, no randomness, fully deterministic).

input_specification.format: in-memory Python objects (lists/dicts/strings) constructed within the notebook cell, no file or network I/O
input_specification.fields: task-specific records or documents as described in problem_description

output_specification.format: Python list/dict of matching ids or records, returned deterministically (stable sort order where ties occur)

constraints: Python standard library only, no internet access
fully deterministic, no randomness in output ordering
no human interaction required
must run offline in Jupyter or Google Colab

small.notes: quick correctness checks, fits in a single cell run

medium.notes: exercises index construction cost and query throughput

large.notes: exposes naive O(N) per-query scans vs indexed lookups

computational_profile.bottleneck: index construction at large scale; per-query lookup cost dominated by naive linear scan if not indexed

public_tests.description: Normal single-term/single-condition query against a small dataset returns the expected result set.
Empty query (empty string, empty list, or empty filter set) returns an empty result without error.
Issuing the identical query twice in a row returns identical results both times and does not mutate the index.
Query executed against the medium-scale generated dataset returns correct results within expected structure.
Boundary/unusual query (e.g. query term absent from data, or filter values at the extreme min/max) is handled correctly.

hidden_tests.description: Normal multi-condition or multi-term query on a freshly built index returns exactly the expected matches.
Query with all fields/terms empty or None across an otherwise non-empty dataset returns an empty result.
Same query issued 50 times in a loop returns identical, order-stable results every time.
Query executed against the large-scale generated dataset completes and returns correct results, verifying the index is actually used rather than a full rescan.
Unusual query such as a duplicate term repeated within a single query, or a value exactly on a range boundary, is handled per specification.

reference_solution.algorithm: Tokenize each document, build a dict mapping token -> sorted list of document ids (inverted index). Answer queries by set-intersection of postings lists.
reference_solution.time_complexity: O(N*L) to build (N docs, L avg tokens); O(min posting list size) per AND query using intersection
reference_solution.space_complexity: O(V + sum posting lengths) where V is vocabulary size

The solution must be implemented as pure, offline, deterministic Python runnable in a single Jupyter/Colab cell with no network or human interaction.
functional_requirements: R1: Correctly build the required index/data structure described for 'Multi-Keyword Search with Mixed AND/OR Groups' from the given input collection.
R2: Correctly answer a single query against the built structure, returning results in the specified deterministic order.
R3: Correctly handle an empty query or empty input collection by returning an empty result rather than raising an exception.
R4: Support repeated/duplicate queries returning consistent results without mutating the underlying index.
R5: Scale to large input sizes without falling back to a full linear rescan per query where an index lookup is specified by the algorithm.
R6: Return results using only the documented input/output types (no extra I/O, no randomness, fully deterministic).

reference_solution.algorithm: Sort entries by timestamp for binary-search range slicing, and build a level->set(index) map; combine range result indices with the level set via intersection.
reference_solution.time_complexity: O(N log N) to build; O(log N + range size) per query
reference_solution.code:
import bisect

def build_indices(entries):
    sorted_entries = sorted(range(len(entries)), key=lambda i: entries[i]["timestamp"])
    sorted_ts = [entries[i]["timestamp"] for i in sorted_entries]
    level_index = {}
    for i, e in enumerate(entries):
        level_index.setdefault(e["level"], set()).add(i)
    return sorted_entries, sorted_ts, level_index

def query(entries, sorted_entries, sorted_ts, level_index, start, end, level):
    lo = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_ts, start)
    hi = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_ts, end)
    range_idx = set(sorted_entries[lo:hi])
    matched = range_idx & level_index.get(level, set())
    return sorted((entries[i] for i in matched), key=lambda e: e["timestamp"]) if False else [entries[i] for i in sorted(matched)]
